the {{ls}}ovver vvent forth to {{ls}}ovv. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=4}} And vvhiles he {{ls}}ovveth, {{ls}}ome fel by the vvay {{ls}}ide, and the foules of the aire came, and did eate it. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=5}} And other{{ls}}ome fel vpon rocky places vvhere it had not much earth: and it {{ls}}hot vp immediatly, becau{{ls}}e it had not deepnes of earth: {{verse|chapter=4|verse=6}} and vvhen the {{ls}}unne was ri{{ls}}en, it parched, and becau{{ls}}e it had not roote, it vvithered. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=7}} And {{ls}}ome fel among thornes: and the thornes grewe vp, and choked it, and it yelded not fruite. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=8}} And {{ls}}ome fel vpon good ground: and it yelded fruite that grewe vp and increa{{ls}}ed, and it brought forth, one thirtie, one {{ls}}ixtie, and one an hundred.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=9}} And he {{ls}}aid, He that hath eares to heare, let him heare. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=10}} And vvhen he vvas alone, the Tvvelue that vvere vvith him, a{{ls}}ked him the parable. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=11}} And he {{ls}}aid to them, To you it is giuen to knovv the my{{ls}}terie of the kingdom of God: but to {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Such as be out of the Church, though they heare and read neuer {{ls}}o much, they cannot vnder{{ls}}tand.
